name: Global temperature
summary: Global temperature 1.99°C above pre-industrial on 5 Nov, a record for the date
state: ERA5 data for 5 Nov put global surface air temperature at 14.83°C, about 1.99°C above pre-industrial levels and a record for the calendar date, above the 1.6°C Alert line (Climate Reanalyzer). The estimate adds 0.88°C to the 1991–2020 anomaly of 1.11°C. Readings over the previous eight days ranged from about 1.89°C to 2.05°C, up from about 1.83°C on 28 Oct, with the strong El Niño adding heat.
for_you: Record global warmth raises the odds of heatwaves, marine heat and heavy rainfall in many regions. For local impacts, follow national met service warnings such as the Met Office.
rubric_hit: Daily anomaly +1.99°C > +1.6°C Alert line, and a record for the date

sources.title: Climate Reanalyzer — Daily global surface air temperature (ERA5)

why: Global temperature is the master climate variable; each tenth of a degree raises extreme-weather risk.
drivers: Greenhouse gases, El Niño/La Niña, aerosols, solar cycle.

rubric.alert: > +1.6°C, or a record high for the calendar date.
rubric.normal: Daily global anomaly < +1.3°C above pre-industrial (ERA5 vs 1991–2020 + 0.88°C).
